name: Burkina Faso

facts.religion: Muslim about 64%, Christian about 26%, traditional faiths

snapshot: A junta led by Captain Ibrahim Traoré, which said it foiled a coup and assassination plot in January 2026 and restored the death penalty in October, while jihadists hold much of the countryside.
culture: Burkina Faso means "land of upright people", a name chosen by the revolutionary leader Thomas Sankara, whose image remains everywhere. Ouagadougou hosts FESPACO, Africa's biggest film festival, every two years, and the Mossi kingdom's Mogho Naba still holds a weekly ceremony at his palace. Bobo-Dioulasso's mud mosque and the country's masked dances reflect a deep mix of Islamic and older traditions.
society: Most people farm or herd, and gold has become the main export. The jihadist insurgency since 2015 has displaced more than two million people and closed thousands of schools. Civilian volunteer militias recruited by the junta have been accused of massacres, especially against Fulani communities. Independent media have been suspended and critics conscripted to the front.
situation: Captain Ibrahim Traoré seized power in September 2022, expelled French troops, brought in Russian security support and, with Mali and Niger, formed the Alliance of Sahel States and left ECOWAS. In January 2026 the junta said it had foiled a coup and a plot to assassinate Traoré, blaming Côte d'Ivoire, and in October its appointed parliament voted to restore the death penalty. The jihadist insurgency keeps killing soldiers and civilians, and rights groups document abuses by both sides. Traoré keeps a large online following across Africa as an anti- colonial figure.
power: Military rule. Traoré is head of state under a transition charter the junta extended in 2024 to run until 2029; an appointed assembly and a prime minister serve at his pleasure.

leaders.gov: Prime Minister Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo
